title: The Clean Border
premise: Quentin Nystrom, a veteran air-crash investigator, has spent three years haunted by the crash that killed her husband and daughter in row twelve — a crash whose official cause she knows is a lie. When the government safe house where she hid the flight's black-box duplicate is listed for sale online, complete with interior photos showing her hidden evidence gone, Quentin realizes someone has found it and is hunting everyone who knows what row twelve really contained. She allies with Mara Voss, the estranged daughter of the whistleblower who planted the evidence, and together they trace the listing to Corliss Dane, a private-security magnate whose company caused the crash and whose fixer is eliminating witnesses. In the end Quentin trades the one secret worth killing for — the identity of the insider who moved the black box — to federal prosecutors in exchange for immunity and protection for Mara, testifying publicly as Dane's network collapses, and finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Edmund Montrose is the pen name of a former aviation-industry analyst who spent a decade inside accident-review boards before walking away. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped between institutional lies and personal grief.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Three years after the Meridian 214 crash, Quentin still sleeps in a chair beside the door of her apartment, insomnia framed through flashbacks of identifying her family's belongings. A routine FOIA denial letter arrives stamped with an unfamiliar private-security logo: Dane-Hallow Group. Emotional beat: grief calcified into vigilance.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Scrolling real-estate sites at 3 a.m., she finds the rural safe house where she once stashed her duplicate of the flight recorder listed for sale — with interior photos showing the crawlspace panel open and empty. Someone knows. She books a rental car before dawn. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Empty Crawlspace
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the safe house she finds fresh tool marks, a discarded coffee cup, and a motion-sensor camera angled at the road — someone watched her arrive. She realizes the listing itself was bait to flush out whoever still had access codes. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. Introduced living under a new name in Portland, Mara receives an anonymous photo of her father's handwriting on the safe house deed. Her father, Elias Voss, was the maintenance engineer who died mysteriously weeks after the crash. Emotional beat: anger at a dead father colliding with fear he left her a legacy.

chapters.title: Two Strangers, One Deed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Quentin traces the listing agent; Mara traces the photo sender; both converge on the same shuttered title office in Spokane. They meet suspiciously in a parking lot, each believing the other may be the enemy. Emotional beat: wary recognition of shared damage.

chapters.title: What Elias Knew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara opens her father's storage unit, finding schematics showing a servo actuator batch knowingly certified by Dane-Hallow despite failed stress tests. Quentin confirms the failure signature matches the crash data she memorized. Emotional beat: the lie takes shape and has a corporate face.

chapters.title: The Fixer
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Renn Sable). Dane-Hallow's cleanup specialist Renn Sable reports to Corliss Dane that two names remain active on the witness ledger: Nystrom and Voss. He requests permission to escalate. Cold, procedural chapter establishing the threat's competence. Emotional beat: menace without malice.

chapters.title: Runlight
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin and Mara flee Spokane as Sable's team closes in, Quentin's counter-surveillance instincts saving them from a tail. First real trust forms when Mara refuses to abandon Quentin's injured shoulder. Emotional beat: found family's first fragile stitch.

chapters.title: The Insider
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Reviewing her old notes, Quentin deduces the black box couldn't have been moved from the safe house without an internal NTSB credential — there is a mole inside the investigation itself, someone who signed off on the official 'pilot error' finding. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the institution she served.

chapters.title: Safe House Burning
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The pair returns to the safe house to recover Elias's second cache and finds it torched; in the ashes, a partial drive survives. Sable nearly catches them; Mara's quick thinking on a farm road buys their escape. Emotional beat: terror tempered by growing partnership.

chapters.title: Dane
chapters.summary: Corliss Dane's POV. Introduced at a charity gala, Dane is charming, principled-seeming, genuinely convinced the recall would have bankrupted thousands of honest employees. He orders Sable to offer Quentin money first, force second. Emotional beat: villainy as reasonable arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Sable approaches Quentin openly with a settlement and a threat wrapped in courtesy: sign the nondisclosure, or Mara dies first. Quentin stalls, recording everything, but realizes the recording means nothing without the original drive authenticated. Emotional beat: fury learning patience.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Decoding her father's cache, Mara finds a recorded call between Elias and the NTSB insider — voice only, no name — plus a dead-drop protocol Elias never completed. The insider is alive and reachable. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as more danger.

chapters.title: The Mole's Face
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Cross-referencing the drop protocol with board rosters, Quentin identifies Deputy Director Alan Reeve — the man who consoled her at the memorial service. Confronting him secretly, she finds him terrified, not loyal: Dane owns him via debts and worse. Emotional beat: disgust braided with pity.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable closes in on Reeve to erase the last link, forcing Quentin and Mara into an impossible choice: protect the traitor who can testify or let him die and lose their case. They save Reeve from Sable's staged suicide setup by minutes. Emotional beat: justice demanding they protect the unworthy.

chapters.title: Trade Wind
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin brokers the deal she swore she'd never make: Reeve's full cooperation and testimony in exchange for her silence about his role until trial. Federal prosecutor Imani Cole agrees to take the case if Quentin can produce physical corroboration within seventy-two hours. Emotional beat: the secret priced, the clock started.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The trio races to authenticate the damaged drive at an independent lab while Sable, tipped off by a leak, prepares interception. Mara and Quentin argue over whether to run abroad instead; Mara chooses to stay — choosing Quentin. Emotional beat: found family solidifying under fire.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Sable's POV then Quentin's. The lab convoy is ambushed on a mountain pass; Quentin uses crash-scene triage instincts to turn the wreck into cover, and Mara disables Sable's vehicle. Sable escapes but the drive survives, chain of custody intact with Cole's agents. Emotional beat: competence as love.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed
chapters.summary: Corliss Dane's POV. With Reeve flipped and the drive authenticated, Dane's board turns on him; he burns records and plans exile, ordering Sable to end all loose ends including, quietly, Sable himself. Emotional beat: the arithmetic failing its accountant.

chapters.title: Hearing Room
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Climax: at the federal hearing, Dane's lawyers attack Quentin's judgment and grief; Sable attempts to intimidate Reeve mid-testimony and is arrested in the hallway. Quentin delivers her account of row twelve — the seat numbers, the servo serial, her daughter's name entered into the record. Emotional beat: grief spoken aloud becomes testimony.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Dane is indicted and Dane-Hallow's certification fraud unravels; a national recall follows. Mara visits her father's grave with the exoneration clipping, and she and Quentin formally become each other's emergency contacts. Emotional beat: mourning finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Through the Night
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Epilogue: months later, Quentin sleeps eight hours in a house with an unlocked door, waking naturally to sunlight and Mara making coffee. A news alert about Dane's trial date passes without flinching. She keeps row twelve's memory — now carried, not carried alone. Emotional beat: rest earned, family chosen.
